claims.quote: Women who have never been sexually active are rarely affected

claims.text: Thin homogeneous discharge that smoothly coats the vaginal walls
claims.quote: Homogeneous, thin discharge (milklike consistency) that smoothly coats the vaginal walls

claims.quote: Treatment for BV is recommended for women with symptoms. Established benefits of therapy among nonpregnant women are to relieve vaginal symptoms and signs of infection.

claims.text: Potential benefits include lower risk of acquiring STIs incl. HIV, HPV, HSV-2; no direct oral vs topical comparison
claims.quote: Other potential benefits of treatment include reduction in the risk for acquiring,,, HIV, HPV, and HSV-2 ... No data are available that directly compare the efficacy of oral and topical medications for treating BV.

claims.quote: Thus, refraining from alcohol use while taking metronidazole (or tinidazole) is unnecessary.

claims.text: Cited review found no convincing evidence of disulfiram-like interaction with metronidazole
claims.quote: A review regarding alcohol consumption during metronidazole treatment reported no in vitro studies, animal models, reports of adverse effects, or clinical studies providing convincing evidence of a disulfiram-like interaction between alcohol and metronidazole

claims.text: No studies support probiotic products as adjunctive or replacement therapy
claims.quote: overall, no studies support these products as an adjunctive or replacement therapy for women with BV

claims.text: Clindamycin cream preferred with metronidazole or tinidazole allergy/intolerance; gel if oral metronidazole not tolerated
claims.quote: Intravaginal clindamycin cream is preferred in case of allergy or intolerance to metronidazole or tinidazole. Intravaginal metronidazole gel can be considered for women who are not allergic to metronidazole but do not tolerate oral metronidazole.

claims.text: All women with BV should be tested for HIV and other STIs
claims.quote: All women with BV should be tested for HIV and other STIs.

claims.text: Return for evaluation if symptoms recur
claims.quote: Because persistent or recurrent BV is common, women should be advised to return for evaluation if symptoms recur.

claims.text: Suppression: twice weekly 0.75% gel or 750 mg suppository >3 months reduces recurrences; benefit does not persist after stopping
claims.quote: either 0.75% metronidazole gel or 750 mg metronidazole vaginal suppository twice weekly for >3 months has been reported to reduce recurrences, although this benefit does not persist when suppressive therapy is discontinued

claims.text: Limited-data option: nitroimidazole 7d, boric acid 600 mg x21d, then twice-weekly gel 4 to 6 months
claims.quote: an oral nitroimidazole (metronidazole or tinidazole 500 mg 2 times/day for 7 days), followed by intravaginal boric acid 600 mg daily for 21 days and suppressive 0.75% metronidazole gel twice weekly for 4–6 months, might be an option

claims.quote: however this medication is not yet FDA cleared or commercially available

claims.text: BV-associated bacteria can be identified on male genitalia
claims.quote: Although BV-associated bacteria can be identified on male genitalia

claims.text: Routine screening of asymptomatic pregnant women not recommended
